## Accessibility

`accessibility` · version 2.0.2 · canonical · [full text](ACCESSIBILITY.md)

The default product already works for different vision, movement and assistive technology. Preferences may add comfort; nothing may drop below this floor (see the floor, rule 14).

Its rules in short (it marks none MUST) ([all the rules](ACCESSIBILITY.md#rules)):

- **1.** Keyboard first-class.
- **2.** Focus visible.
- **3.** Targets at least 44×44 CSS px.
- **4.** Meaning in words.
- **5.** Real structure.
- **6.** Honest names.
- **7.** Errors explain.
- **8.** Zoom never blocked.
- **9.** Text wraps, not clips.
- **10.** Scroll inside the table, not the page.
- **11.** System modes welcomed.
- **12.** Destructive actions named.
- **13.** No fine-motor demands.
- **14.** Dialogs behave.
- **15.** No "accessibility mode".

## Attention and Quiet

`attention-and-quiet` · version 2.0.0 · canonical · [full text](ATTENTION_AND_QUIET.md)

Routine success costs no attention; only things needing a person interrupt. Write down whatever a person would otherwise have to remember. Interruption is normal; coming back must be easy.

Its rules in short (it marks none MUST) ([all the rules](ATTENTION_AND_QUIET.md#rules)):

- **1.** Exceptions get attention.
- **2.** Announce changes, not observations.
- **3.** "Nothing needed" is a state.
- **4.** Quiet means checked.
- **5.** Batch the routine.
- **6.** No manufactured urgency.
- **7.** Don't store state in people.
- **8.** First screen answers three questions.
- **9.** Shape the reading load.
- **10.** Progress persists as it happens.
- **11.** Leaving is always safe.
- **12.** Returning costs no archaeology.
- **13.** Handoffs work cold.
- **14.** Announcements are polite.

## Depth on Demand

`depth-on-demand` · version 2.1.0 · canonical · [full text](DEPTH_ON_DEMAND.md)

Keep the depth; control when it shows. Smallest useful amount first, honest steps down to full detail, and an optional guided path for genuinely complex flows. Familiar explanations and analogies may help someone enter; they never replace the path to the real system.

Its rules in short (it marks none MUST) ([all the rules](DEPTH_ON_DEMAND.md#rules)):

- **1.** Organize complexity, don't delete it.
- **2.** First view stands alone.
- **3.** No dead-end summaries.
- **4.** Disclosure is for depth, not secrets.
- **5.** One disclosure mechanism.
- **6.** No forced complexity.
- **7.** Lead with human meaning.
- **8.** Depth is open to everyone.
- **9.** Guides are optional.
- **10.** No wizards for everything.
- **11.** Steps are real and verified.
- **12.** Guides survive interruption.
- **13.** Docs climb the same ladder.
- **14.** Scaffolding leads to bedrock.

## Human Reliability

`human-reliability` · version 2.0.0 · canonical · [full text](HUMAN_RELIABILITY.md)

No heroics required: a tired, interrupted or unfamiliar person operates the system correctly. The system holds the complexity; the person holds the judgment.

Its rules in short (it marks none MUST) ([all the rules](HUMAN_RELIABILITY.md#rules)):

- **1.** No heroics.
- **2.** Unnecessary cognitive load is technical debt.
- **3.** Choose the reliable default
- **4.** Write for a strained reader.
- **5.** A calm surface never hides truth.
- **6.** Never imply obligation.
- **7.** Make pushback cheap and honored.
- **8.** Put checking in the machine.

## Sensory Safety

`sensory-safety` · version 2.0.0 · canonical · [full text](SENSORY_SAFETY.md)

Start still: no flashing, no ambient motion, no unasked sound. Motion is allowed only when it means something, stays short, and always has a static version.

Its rules in short (it marks none MUST) ([all the rules](SENSORY_SAFETY.md#rules)):

- **1.** Never flash or strobe.
- **2.** Calm by default.
- **3.** Loading is static.
- **4.** Nothing moves on its own.
- **5.** Motion that means something.
- **6.** The system wins.
- **7.** Motion carries no exclusive meaning.
- **8.** Acting gets feedback.
- **9.** Feedback tells the truth.
- **10.** Success is quiet.
- **11.** Sound and vibration are opt-in.
- **12.** Comfort never lowers the floor.

## Themes and Personalization

`themes-and-personalization` · version 2.0.0 · canonical · [full text](THEMES_AND_PERSONALIZATION.md)

Let people make it theirs. One stack decides who wins: the floor, then packs, then project, then personal preferences, then theme. Nothing lower breaks what is above.

Its rules in short (it marks none MUST) ([all the rules](THEMES_AND_PERSONALIZATION.md#rules)):

- **1.** One authority stack.
- **2.** Every theme ships on the floor.
- **3.** Comfort has a lane.
- **4.** No "accessibility mode".
- **5.** Decoration stays decoration.
- **6.** Themes leave cleanly.
- **7.** Core owns semantics.
- **8.** Presentation only.
- **9.** Preferences belong to the person.
- **10.** The floor is structural.

## What, Why, Next

`what-why-next` · version 2.0.0 · canonical · [full text](WHAT_WHY_NEXT.md)

Every important state and message answers: what happened, why it matters, what's next — including "nothing needed". Done is a real state: say it, mean it, keep it.

Its rules in short (it marks none MUST) ([all the rules](WHAT_WHY_NEXT.md#rules)):

- **1.** Answer the three questions.
- **2.** "Nothing needed" is a first-class answer.
- **3.** Information design, not layout.
- **4.** State, then reason, then action.
- **5.** Use the reader's words.
- **6.** Errors keep the shape.
- **7.** Reports inherit it.
- **8.** Progress means getting closer.
- **9.** Done is said, and it sticks.
- **10.** Defer visibly.
- **11.** Let people finish.
- **12.** Progress displays tell the truth.
